We start by changing the variable:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =3{x}^{2}+1 \\ \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =6x \\ \text{d}u & =6x\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{1}{6}\,\text{d}u & =x\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we create a table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=3{x}^{2}+1.$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & 0 & 1 \\ u & 1 & 4\end{aligned}
$$

So, the integral in terms of the new variable is

$$
{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{3{x}^{2}+1}\cdot x\,\text{d}x={\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{6}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we can solve it and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{6}\,\text{d}u & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡(u){|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
